title: Photon-Counting CT-Arthrography of Wrists Suspected of Soft Tissue Injuries
summary:
In cases of hand or wrist complaints, hand surgeons frequently recommend wrist arthroscopy to identify and treat soft-tissue injuries. Prior to this procedure, CT arthrography—performed using a state-of-the-art computed tomography scanner (Photon-Counting CT or PCCT)—helps to better characterize the symptoms, thereby enabling targeted arthroscopic intervention and, where appropriate, treatment.
This is an observational study investigating the diagnostic accuracy of modern Photon-Counting CT arthrography for acute and degenerative soft-tissue injuries of the wrist and carpus. We are analyzing the impact of implementing PCCT at the Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin with the aim of developing modern approaches to quality assurance.
conditions: Traumatic rupture of ligament of wrist and carpus

interventions.name: Prospective enrollment of 200 patients presenting consecutively with suspected acute or degenerative soft-tissue injuries of the carpus or wrist, for whom—based on clinical findings, mechanism of injury, and available imaging—there is an indication for arthroscopy and, potentially, surgical interven

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Suspected acute and degenerative soft-tissue injuries of the carpus or wrist
- Indication for arthroscopy and, if applicable, surgical intervention
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to consent, age under 18, pregnancy, and withdrawal of consent.
